why: The abandoned warehouse in the Northside docks is the Maelstrom stash where Sacrum Profanum stages the captured monk's brother: a fenced, container-ringed yard with a covered hall, a gate access point, security cameras and a restricted-area controller. The job itself never happens in our timeline, so nobody is abducted; the venue should simply read as a working Maelstrom den. This proposal loads #mq032_pr_sacrum (the quest prefab that carries the gang's spawner and its nine named AI spots) and activates the five vanilla Maelstrom entries in their only phase, 'default': cigarettes, a bottle, dancing, patrolling and standing about. No variant toggles are needed and the building shell is world-streamed.

open_questions: Check that the five Maelstrom are inside the yard on their idle spots (cigarette, dancing, drinking, standing, patrolling) and not clustered at the spawner or frozen mid-pose. The catalogue rates this community posture unknown because its community-area node is in always_loaded_0 while its spots are in the quest sector; I resolved the mapping by hand.

Walk in through the front gate and confirm the stash is enterable, then check the south grate gives the Technical Ability prompt and slides open. The hatch is a world entity, not a quest door, so the runtime door policy will not touch it.
Confirm loading #mq032_pr_sacrum adds only spawners, spots and trigger areas: no captive monk, no Johnny, no rescue props, and no job objective should appear when the prefab loads.

Check the crew's attitude on approach. They are Maelstrom and may turn hostile when the player enters the yard; confirm that reads as a normal gang stash and not as the job's combat scene (an empty, silent yard would be the failure).

communities.why: The warehouse's own Maelstrom crew, not a quest-only appearance: the community area node assigns this entry a vanilla cigarette-smoke spot in the yard. vanilla activates the same entry/phase from the combat phase; the phase itself is an idle spot set (the hostility in the job comes from the quest graph, not the phase), so activating it outside the job gives a ganger leaning and smoking at the stash.
Second of the stash crew; its mapped spot plays the homeless dance-freak animation beside the yard, i.e. a ganger goofing off at the den, not a combat pose.
Third crew member; its mapped spot is a bottle-drink stance by the hall, the sort of idle beat that makes the stash look lived in.
Fourth crew member; its mapped spot is a plain dirt stand-around in the yard, a second body on watch by the containers.

Fifth crew member, the one who walks a patrol line (patrolling_stand) along the container side of the yard; together with the other four this is the full vanilla set the combat phase uses, so no extra or invented ganger is added.

proximity_wait.why: The gate network access point, 9.6 m from the crew's spots: an authored worldDeviceNode in the gameplay prefab (exterior_-34_44_0_0) that streams with the venue and is a device, not a workspot, so the proximity wait can fire. The catalogue's own device entries are unusable (ref 0, path null, venue_inferred): they are the SecurityAreaControllerPS actions mq032_02_maelstrom fires inside the unloaded quest graph.
